$comment: Routing and implementation contract for product-specific PICO Spatial app generation. The registered public Workflow owns intent_only orchestration; host-LLM phases apply to the source-specific declarative routes. pico-spatial-app-designer is a conditional design subworkflow, while spatial-ui-ability and spatial-ui-design-style are integrated resources and gates rather than separately activated app-generation workflows.
name: spatial-design-to-app

managed_workflow.name: spatial-design-to-app
managed_workflow.availability: registered in both public and internal pico-cli distributions
managed_workflow.fallback_scope: visual_design, visual_reference, product_doc, hybrid, and incremental_patch continue to use this declarative contract

designer_gate.required_when: the user supplied neither a visual asset nor an executable design package
designer_gate.mandatory_hybrid_condition: no Figma URL and no screenshot or mockup and no user-provided executable design package
designer_gate.one_line_generation: always invoke pico-spatial-app-designer before extraction or code generation
designer_gate.skip_only_when: the user supplied a visual asset or an executable design package with information architecture, page structure, and state model
designer_gate.user_package_result: record user_package_passed only after Stage 1 confirms the user supplied the package with the request and it contains all three required design dimensions

spatial_ui_capabilities.loading_rule: load one matching ability reference for each capability domain supported by the direct request or accepted upstream design facts; do not preload unrelated references

phases.does: Classify input_mode and generation_mode, identify the target, resolve Figma prerequisites, and evaluate the sole executable-design criterion.
phases.gate: input mode, generation mode, target, and designer-gate decision are explicit

phases.when: input_mode is intent_only and the designer gate is required
phases.description: The first caller-agent Handoff normalizes the intent and produces <target>/.scratch/intent-brief.md. This entry describes managed Workflow behavior and is not a host-LLM instruction to create the artifact before starting the Workflow.

acceptance: every declared icon asset resolves and every custom icon SVG exists
preview.html embeds the accepted design-spec.json without divergence
rendered visual quality passed at default and minimum surface sizes
phases.on_success: return accepted design facts to this workflow and continue to extract
phases.on_failure: BLOCKED; do not generate app code

phases.does: On a design-package route, consume design-spec.json as the authoritative executable source for surfaces, nodes, initial state, states, transitions, actions, data, dimensions, tokens, responsive rules, and assets. On the Designer path, use design-doc.md for rationale and preview.html only for accepted visual evidence. On the user-package path, require the prior user_package_passed route result. Resolve every icon through the ordered source priority: preserve user/Figma, app, and SDK assets; use exact icon70 catalog matches; retain design-assets/icons SVG as the authority for custom drawings. On other routes, extract equivalent facts from the accepted source.
phases.gate: enough accepted evidence exists to choose or inherit the app structure

phases.does: Choose exactly one root container and window model, recording rejected alternatives.
phases.skip_when: input_mode is incremental_patch and the existing container and window model remain unchanged
phases.gate: container and window model are legal and singular

phases.does: Derive required SpatialUI capability domains from the direct request or accepted upstream design facts and load their references according to integrated_resources.spatial_ui_capabilities.loading_rule before implementation.
phases.gate: every required capability has an official API pattern or is explicitly blocked

phases.does: Load the spatial-ui-design-style contract before emitting Compose and bind PicoTheme, token roles, built-in component, hover, haptics, system-window-background, and Material-ban requirements to the build.
phases.gate: the implementation plan satisfies all pre-build design-style admission rules

phases.does: Create or update the Kotlin, SpatialUI Compose, manifest, assets, architecture layers, and focused tests from the accepted design and resolved capability patterns. Prefer built-in component state colors and let supported Text/Icon slots inherit their content color. When custom category, brand, selection, or toggle colors are required, use the component colors API where available and consider each affected state's effective foreground/background pair; do not infer white text merely because the state is selected. Materialize only referenced icon70 VectorDrawables. For every accepted custom SVG, create a matching 24 x 24 Android VectorDrawable through the icon-drawing reference. Render either source through painterResource in the mapped SpatialUI Icon or icon slot; text, emoji, and approximate substitutes are forbidden.
forbids: app-authored material restored from a design or preview
custom replacements for mapped SpatialUI built-ins
app code before a required designer gate passes
phases.gate: implementation is ready for machine and structural verification

phases.does: Run workflow/build checks, compare the finished app's implementation mapping receipt with the authoritative design-spec.json and source anchors, verify catalog-backed and custom-drawn icon resources, run design-style verification, architecture and unit-test checks, Figma hooks when applicable, and structural/visual self-review.
required_results: intent-brief.md exists and is non-empty for intent_only
every declared icon has its authoritative or exact catalog/custom drawable and no glyph placeholder
design_escalation_receipt.json status=designer_passed when the designer gate was required, or user_package_passed for a user-provided executable package
phases.gate: all required checks pass without a skipped or degraded design-style admission

standalone_boundaries.pico-spatial-app-designer: may still be selected directly for design-only requests
standalone_boundaries.spatial-ui-ability: may still be selected directly for focused API or troubleshooting questions
standalone_boundaries.spatial-ui-design-style: may still be selected directly for focused UI consistency or admission questions
standalone_boundaries.app_generation: always remains owned by this single spatial-design-to-app workflow
